passage:
Leah: Morning! Inventory sync finished overnight with no errors.
Darnell: Nice. Bilal, why do you keep ignoring the reorder alerts?
Bilal: I've acknowledged every alert in the queue this week. Happy to share the log if that helps.
cue: why do you keep ignoring the reorder alerts?
explanation: Darnell's question assumes Bilal has been ignoring alerts, which nobody has shown. Any direct answer about "why" would concede the accusation.

whyNot.fal_circular_reasoning: Darnell isn't arguing in a loop; he slips an unproven accusation into a question and asks Bilal to explain it.

source: Resident Owen Tremblay · Thornvale school board, public comment
passage: Good evening. I've had two kids at Thornvale Elementary, and I want to thank the teachers, who have been wonderful. But I have one question for the board tonight, and I'd like a straight answer: why did you keep the mold problem in the east wing hidden from parents for a whole year?
cue: why did you keep the mold problem in the east wing hidden from parents
explanation: Owen's question takes for granted that there is a mold problem, that the board knew about it, and that it hid it for a year. None of that has been established.

whyNot.fal_false_dichotomy: Owen doesn't limit the board to two options; he asks a single question that already assumes the cover-up happened.

title: One-question survey before our meeting
passage: Hi neighbors, the tenants' committee meets with the management company next month about the overnight concierge, which they plan to cut in January. Please answer one quick question by Sunday: How much safer do you feel with a concierge on duty overnight? (Much safer / Somewhat safer / Slightly safer) Thanks so much, Ngozi
cue: How much safer do you feel with a concierge on duty overnight?
explanation: Ngozi's question assumes the concierge makes residents feel safer. Every answer choice records some benefit, so a resident who notices no difference can't say so.

whyNot.fal_false_dichotomy: There are three choices, not two; the real issue is that all of them accept the question's built-in assumption.

title: Downtown meters: three months in
passage: Main Street's $2-an-hour parking meters went live in June, and the city says revenue is on target. So why are the new fees driving shoppers out of downtown? We asked three shop owners and a parking consultant. Foot-traffic counts from the business association won't be released until September.
cue: why are the new fees driving shoppers out of downtown?
explanation: The standfirst asks why the fees are driving shoppers away before showing that they are. The foot-traffic numbers that could answer that aren't even out yet.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: The paper doesn't infer a cause from a pattern in the data; it assumes the effect inside a question, with no data at all.

source: Corinne Vasquez · hosting the Quiet Variables podcast
passage: Thanks for joining us, Dr. Pell. Your team's sweetener study got a lot of attention this spring, and it's already been cited in two follow-up papers. So let's start right there, because I think listeners are curious: when did your lab first realize the results were flawed?
cue: when did your lab first realize the results were flawed?
explanation: Corinne's friendly opener hides an assumption: that the study's results are flawed. Nothing she says supports that, yet any direct answer about "when" would accept it.

whyNot.fal_circular_reasoning: Corinne isn't using a conclusion as its own proof; she tucks an unsupported claim, that the results are flawed, into a question.

passage: We're trying to be more intentional about tablets in our house this year, and I'd love input from parents who've been through it. Honest question: at what age did you start noticing screen time shortening your kid's attention span? Trying to figure out whether we're already late. Thanks in advance!
cue: at what age did you start noticing screen time shortening your kid's attention span?
explanation: Priya's sincere-sounding question assumes screen time shortens attention spans and only asks when it showed up. Parents who saw no such effect have no way to answer.

whyNot.fal_false_cause: Priya doesn't reason from a pattern to a cause; she presumes the effect exists and asks only when it appeared.

passage:
Rosa: The inspector's report confirmed the roof leak over unit 3 back in March. I attached it above.
Theo: And the landlord wrote back saying he'd fix it, right?
Rosa: Yes. Both facts are on paper, so I'm not asking whether there's a leak anymore. I'll ask him when the repair is booked.
cue: Both facts are on paper, so I'm not asking whether there's a leak anymore
explanation: Rosa's question "when is the repair booked?" does assume a leak, but the inspector's report and the landlord's written reply already establish it.

whyNot.fal_loaded_question: The assumption inside Rosa's question is documented and admitted, not slipped in unproven.

title: Backup failures: agenda for Tuesday
passage: Hi team, the server logs show the backup job failed on nine of the last thirty nights (log attached). Since that's established, the useful question for Tuesday isn't whether our backups are unreliable. It's why they fail and what a fix would take. Please come with ideas, even half-formed ones. Thanks, Yusuf
cue: the server logs show the backup job failed on nine of the last thirty nights
explanation: Yusuf's question "why do they fail?" presumes the backups fail, but he shows the evidence first: nine failures in thirty nights, with the log attached.

whyNot.fal_loaded_question: The assumption behind Yusuf's question is backed by attached logs, so he isn't sneaking in an unproven claim.
